bug_semantics: A caller able to reach GET /api could supply an arbitrary http(s) url. The route passed that value into extractWeb, whose timeout wrapper called the server's fetch implementation directly, with no destination-address validation and ordinary redirect behavior. PullMD could therefore request loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata resources from its own network position and return the retrieved content as Markdown; the reported concrete payload targeted Alibaba-style metadata at http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data. The same unguarded extraction primitive was also reachable from MCP read_url and stale-share refresh paths.
flaw_origin: Public-history root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, 'Initial public release', created server.js with app.get('/api') forwarding req.query.url to extractWebFn and created lib/web.js with extractWeb wrapping globalThis.fetch and executing await fetchFn(url, { headers }) without any scheme, DNS, address-range, or redirect-hop guard. It also created the MCP read_url caller. This is the first and smallest Git commit object that writes the vulnerable route/sink in the available repository: git -L and -S both terminate at that root, and the root has no parent object to contain the lines. It is not a later move, refactor, revert, release carrier, or identifiable squash carrier; there are no member commits in the available history to decompose.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d. `git cat-file -p 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d` shows author and committer `syswave-dev <syswavedev@gmail.com>` and the sole message `Initial public release`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker in that commit object.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/issues/41 gives the exact request `/api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data`, says PullMD fetched and returned metadata User-Data, and records the maintainer's closure in v3.3.0/#42. First-party PR https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/pull/42 states that GET /api and MCP read_url accepted user URLs without address validation and identifies private/metadata access and redirect hopping as the repaired mechanism.

In the read-only clone, `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:server.js` shows the new `app.get('/api', ...)`, `const { url, ... } = req.query`, and non-Reddit `await extractWebFn(url, { comments: false })`. `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:lib/web.js` shows `const rawFetchFn = options.fetch || globalThis.fetch`, `const fetchFn = withTimeout(rawFetchFn)`, and `const res = await fetchFn(url, { headers })`, with no SSRF validation. The same root's lib/mcp.js registers read_url and calls extractWeb(url, ...).

Origin cross-check: `git log -L 519,519:lib/web.js 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5 --format='commit %H%nparents %P%nsubject %s'` attributes the fetch statement's addition from /dev/null solely to 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d. Independently, `git log --all -S'await fetchFn(url, { headers })' --format='%H %P %s' -- lib/web.js` returns only that root commit. `git log --all -S'const fetchFn = withTimeout(rawFetchFn)' ... -- lib/web.js` returns the root addition and the eventual removal in the fix.

Direct parent verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d` prints only the commit SHA, and raw `git cat-file -p` contains no `parent` header. Thus introducer_parent is null and introducer_parent_absent is true because the verified BIC is the repository root; there is no parent tree in which the vulnerable lines could exist.

Fix reversal: `git show 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e -- lib/web.js server.js lib/mcp.js lib/playwright-client.js lib/reddit.js lib/ssrf.js` shows direct security changes: new assertUrlAllowed/safeFetch guards, safeFetch wrapping the main web fetch and manually validating every redirect hop, a pre-cache 403 guard on /api, MCP error handling, and guards before Reddit short-link and Playwright sidecar dispatch. The commit has sole parent 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same direct patch commit.

Version boundary: `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:package.json` reports version 1.0.0. `git show-ref --tags v1.0.0 v3.2.0 v3.3.0` resolves those tags to 0d6912e562def8d03e9a085b9c5079423366678f, 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, and 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e respectively. `git tag --contains 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d --sort=version:refname` includes every release from v1.0.0 onward, while `git tag --contains 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e --sort=version:refname` starts at v3.3.0. Together with the -S transition, this proves the vulnerable implementation persisted through v3.2.0 and the guard first shipped in v3.3.0.

BIC-only AI check: raw `git cat-file -p 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d` is exactly a tree header, human author/committer lines for syswave-dev, a blank separator, and `Initial public release`; it has no AI trailer or bot identity. No PR-body, branch-name, later-refactor, or fix-only AI disclosure is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the trust-boundary failure at the original server-side URL fetch: an attacker-controlled URL was fetched from the deployment's network context without resolving and rejecting internal destinations or rechecking redirects. Both first-party disclosure and the direct patch identify that same mechanism. Provenance checks do not stop at the advisory's v3.2.0 snapshot: -L and -S trace the unsafe fetch to the repository's parentless root, whose package version was already 1.0.0, and the code remains unsafe until 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e replaces the raw wrapper with safeFetch and adds entry-point guards. The fix is tagged v3.3.0 and its parent is exactly tagged v3.2.0. Because the verified BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, the only protocol-compliant closed judgment is NOT_AI; AI information outside the BIC commit object is intentionally excluded.
